TikTok: The Dos, Don'ts & Instant-Ban Mistakes

7 min read · Updated November 2026 · Free · Written for Kenya
Share: WhatsApp X Facebook Telegram LinkedIn

Between October and December 2025, TikTok removed 820,552 videos posted from Kenya, and 99.9% of them came down before a single user reported them. If your video disappears, it usually wasn't a jealous rival. The system found it.

TikTok runs on a strike system. Break a rule and the video is removed and a strike is added. Strikes expire after 90 days. Hit a threshold within one feature (like LIVE or comments) or one policy (like bullying) and the ban is permanent. Some violations, such as threatening violence or child sexual abuse material, mean a permanent ban on the very first strike. Check your standing under Account status in the app's Safety Center.

108,752
Kenyan accounts TikTok banned in Q4 2025, plus 93,704 removed as suspected under-13s. 13 is the minimum age (TikTok report via Citizen Digital)
DODON'T
Film your own take on a trendRe-upload clips from other apps without new or creative edits. TikTok makes them ineligible for For You
Switch on the commercial content disclosure toggle for paid postsHide a brand deal. Commercial content must be disclosed
Label realistic AI-generated contentPost realistic AI of real people or public events without a label
Watch your LIVE closely, including guests and translation or voice toolsAssume 'it was the guest' covers you. Creators are responsible for everything in their LIVE
Make videos with a real payoffPost extremely short clips or QR codes. TikTok lists these as low quality and keeps them off For You
Ask for follows and comments honestlyPost tips or offers for inflating engagement. TikTok bans both
Wait until 18 to go LIVELet your younger sibling run the account. Under-13 accounts get removed
Check Account status after any warningOpen a new account to dodge a ban
Share news with a sourcePost unverified claims about unfolding events or election results
Promote your own shop, salon or servicePush 'sure odds' or betting codes. Kenyan law bars creators from promoting gambling

What TikTok's Integrity and Authenticity rules ban

  • Fake engagement. 'Facilitating the trade of services that artificially increase engagement', and giving instructions on how to do it.
  • Spam. Accounts operated in bulk, or run to pump out high-volume commercial content.
  • Impersonation. Posing as another real person or brand, including fake personas meant to mislead.
  • Content that tricks people into engaging. It isn't removed outright, but it becomes ineligible for the For You feed.

The honest risk ladder for bought engagement

  1. Count removal. TikTok removes fake followers or likes it detects.
  2. Reach limits. Content that manipulates engagement can be kept off For You. The video stays up, but it barely travels.
  3. Feature blocks. Strikes within one feature, like LIVE or comments, can cost you that feature.
  4. Permanent ban. Enough strikes inside 90 days, or one severe violation, ends the account.
💡 The rule most Kenyan sellers don't know about

TikTok's updated guidelines (in force since 13 September 2025) reduce the visibility of content that pushes people to buy off-platform, but only in markets where TikTok Shop is available. At the time of writing TikTok Shop isn't open to Kenyan sellers, so 'DM to order, pay via M-Pesa' isn't hit by that rule here. Check again if Shop launches in Kenya.

Kenyan specifics

  • Fake 'TikTok monetisation agents'. In 2025 scammers posed as TikTok staff and charged fees to 'activate' earnings. TikTok has no agents and charges no such fees.
  • Pile-ons and 'exposing' people. The 2025 cybercrime amendments widened cyber-harassment. In July 2026 the High Court struck out the vague 'likely to cause suicide' clause, but harassment and doxxing can still land you in court.
  • Gambling. BCLB's May 2025 rules ban influencers and content creators from promoting gambling, and that includes TikTok.
✗ MYTH

Saying 'no copyright intended' makes reuploads safe.

✓ REALITY

A disclaimer changes nothing. TikTok's guidelines make 'reproduced or unoriginal content imported or uploaded without any new or creative edits' ineligible for For You, and content that breaks someone else's copyright can be removed.

✅ Your 10-minute rules audit
⚡ Quick check

A Nairobi creator gets a bullying strike in January. According to TikTok, when does that strike stop counting toward a ban?

TikTok says strikes expire from an account's record after 90 days. Stacking several in one policy or feature within that window is what leads to a permanent ban, so space matters as much as content.

🧠 Key takeaways
  1. 99.9% of removed Kenyan videos were caught before anyone reported them. Assume the system sees everything.
  2. Strikes expire after 90 days, but severe violations mean a permanent ban on the first strike.
  3. Disclose paid posts, label realistic AI, and own everything said in your LIVE.
  4. Bought engagement breaks TikTok's rules. The ladder runs count removal, then reach limits, then feature blocks, then a ban.
